question: What reason justifies conforming to former life-stage conventions despite ended bondage?
premises: There is regard for former life-stages.
This ended state functions as a causal consideration.
inference: Conformity is justified by regard for former stages even when worldly bondage has ended.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation between astasaṃsāra and hetutaḥ is compressed and may link to the next verse.
plain_english: This is because of regard for the former stages of life, even though worldly bondage has ended.
